title: Japan, East Asian Developmental States and the Cold War Global System
summary: Japan's postwar reconfiguration and East Asian developmental states show how state capacity, industrial policy, education, external markets and security conditions can combine in different ways. At the same time, the Cold War embedded regional development within wider structures of security, trade and institutional competition.

blocks.text: Japan's postwar reconfiguration and East Asian developmental states show how state capacity, industrial policy, education, external markets and security conditions can combine in different ways. At the same time, the Cold War embedded regional development within wider structures of security, trade and institutional competition.

No single developmental combination is treated as a template that can simply be copied. Historical starting points, international environments, population structures and institutions differ, so similar tools can produce different outcomes.

This article distinguishes historical fact, historical reconstruction and structural interpretation in the manuscript. Later outcomes are not treated as inevitable at the time, and motives or causal claims not present in the manuscript are not added.
